items.problem: The bootstrap destroyed the scaffold activation manifest and the validator/diagnostic path could not identify the remaining entry-point failure.
items.evidence: lessons.json packaging/startup struggle; migration-score.json candidate_launch_status; active manifest EntryPoint="LinguisticServices.App".
items.root_cause: Tier-1 automation contradicted the correct Tier-3 manifest guidance and omitted a falsifiable entry-point check and managed stack.
items.change: Keep the scaffold manifest active, preserve the UWP manifest as reference, validate $targetentrypoint$, retain managed stack frames, and classify wrong-thread COMException messages specifically. Tier 1 was chosen because prose already existed and was ignored/undermined by tooling.
items.expected_effect: Packaged migrations retain a valid WinUI activation contract and startup failures name an actionable managed frame instead of a generic CLR hint.
items.falsifiable_check: On rerun, bootstrap leaves scaffold Package.appxmanifest active; validator fails any literal UWP App EntryPoint before launch; a wrong-thread crash result contains a non-empty stack and RPC_E_WRONG_THREAD hint.

items.problem: Directory copying omitted linked shared inputs and concealed a native runtime dependency.
items.evidence: lessons.json source-discovery struggle; source csproj linked items and RuntimeComponent.vcxproj.
items.root_cause: Bootstrap modeled filesystem containment rather than MSBuild dependency closure.
items.change: Import external Compile/Page/ApplicationDefinition/Content items to their Link targets and stop explicitly on non-C# ProjectReference dependencies. Tier 1 is necessary because templates/prose cannot reliably reconstruct an arbitrary project graph.
items.expected_effect: Shared source, XAML, and assets enter mapping automatically, while unsupported mixed-language closure is surfaced before lossy substitutions.
items.falsifiable_check: A linked-item fixture produces target files at every Link path and mapping rows for them; a vcxproj ProjectReference terminates bootstrap with the dependency path.

items.problem: Build instructions invoked a nonexistent command.
items.root_cause: Tier-3 guidance confused benchmark nomenclature with standalone CLI capabilities.
items.change: Replace winapp build with dotnet build using an explicit csproj path. No Tier-1/2 change is needed because dotnet already provides the correct build tool and the defect is solely the command text.
items.expected_effect: The first build executes successfully from parent target directories and launch remains delegated to Test-AppLaunch.
items.falsifiable_check: A rerun contains no 'build was not matched' output and the first compile command is dotnet build with a csproj path.
